angle: LongMemEval results claimed by memory systems, 2025-2026, checked against primary sources: the original paper's baselines, vendor and academic claims of 85% or higher, retrieval-only "100%" claims, and third-party reruns. I did no local compute and downloaded no datasets. The only file fetched was the LongMemEval arXiv PDF, which the web tool cached automatically so I could read Tables 3-4 and Figures 3 and 6.

The paper never reports one end-to-end number combining round/session values, fact expansion, time-aware expansion and a CoN reader. The table says 'Recall' without saying whether it is recall_any or recall_all; the released eval_utils.py computes both.

key_takeaways: Engram, confirmed. Its '100%' is a retrieval hit rate: at least one gold session appears among the 60 retrieved memories (~17.7k of ~101.6k tokens), on the 470 answerable questions. Its 90.8% (454/500) is answer accuracy on all 500 questions, answered by claude-sonnet-4-6 and graded by a claude-opus-4-8 judge using a custom rubric, not the official GPT-4o prompts. The two numbers are different metrics with different denominators.

Three kinds of numbers get mixed up in marketing. (1) Session-level recall_any@k, no LLM involved: MemPalace 96.6% at k=5, rohitg00/agentmemory 95.2% at 5, Supermemory 95% at 15 and 97% at 20, Engram 100% at 60 memories. The official retrieval eval skips the 30 abstention questions (n=470); MemPalace and agentmemory say they use 500. (2) LLM-judged answer accuracy on 500 questions. (3) Per-category scores. Supermemory's current research page places its Recall@20 next to Zep's answer accuracy.

The original paper's anchors, verified from the PDF. Full-context GPT-4o on S: 0.606 (0.640 with Chain-of-Note). Oracle GPT-4o: 0.870 (0.924 with JSON + Chain-of-Note). The best end-to-end RAG number is on LongMemEval_M, not S: 0.720 with GPT-4o reading the top 10 rounds, fact-expanded keys, Stella V5 retriever. Time-aware expansion is reported only as retrieval recall on the temporal subset (session R@10 0.721 → 0.797), with no end-to-end number and no single fully combined configuration. The '60.2% full context' and '82.4% oracle' that vendors quote come from Zep's and Emergence's own reruns, not from the paper.

Judges differ widely, so scores are not comparable. Official GPT-4o prompts: Zep, Supermemory, Mastra, Honcho, Chronos, JordanMcCann/agentmemory, TiMem. Other judges: GPT-OSS-120B (Hindsight paper); gemini-2.5-flash-lite, reportedly told to 'be generous' (AMB, 94.6%); GPT-4o-mini with or without auxiliary judges (MemOS, EverMemOS, OmniMemEval, Backboard); Claude Sonnet 4 (Memanto); Claude Opus (Engram); Gemini 3 Flash (ByteRover). Some systems grade themselves with their own reader model: OMEGA (GPT-4.1) and Maximem (gpt-5-mini). Mastra measured ~10-point swings from judge prompt choice alone.

The reader model now dominates. Honcho reports Gemini 3 Pro with the full ~115k context alone at 92.0%, versus 92.6% with Honcho. Emergence reports o3 at 76.0% full-context and 92.0% oracle. Haiku 4.5 alone scores 62.6% full-context and 89.2% oracle. Most 90-96% claims use frontier readers (gpt-5-mini, gpt-5.5, Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.x) and should be compared against a full-context baseline with the same reader.

Adversarial reruns come out far lower. MemTensor's OmniMemEval (reader gpt-4.1-mini, judge gpt-4o-mini, cleaned S) scores Hindsight 72.2 (self-reported 91.4-94.6), Supermemory 66.07 (self-reported 81.6-85.86), Mem0 56.0 (self-reported 94.4), Letta 77.67, and graphiti-zep 79.8 at 117k context tokens, which is effectively full context. The same harness gives MemTensor's own MemOS 89.2 with 100% on all three single-session categories.

Current top self-reported answer accuracies on S: JordanMcCann/agentmemory 96.2% (Opus 4.6 reader, official GPT-4o judge, result JSON committed). Chronos High 95.6% (Opus 4.6; no code). Agent Zero 95.6% (gpt-5.5; judge unnamed; no code). OMEGA 95.4% (self-judged). Mem0 94.4-94.8%. Mastra OM 94.87% (gpt-5-mini). Hindsight 94.6% on AMB. Backboard 93.4%. ByteRover 92.8%. Chronos Low 92.6% (GPT-4o). Maximem 92.0%. Honcho 90.4%. Memanto 89.8%. Emergence 86.0% (GPT-4o). Supermemory's ~99% was a self-declared parody. MemPalace's 100% was tuned on the test set and corrected to 98.4% R@5 on 450 held-out questions.
